note: Adapted from the new-species description in the Journal of the Washington Academy of Sciences 15(19): 443-444, 1925, originally in English. The original describes the soldier only (holotype a soldier, Cat. No. 15297, MCZ, from Ugi Island, Solomon Islands, collected together with workers); the worker and the alate are not described. The author and the title of the paper are not in the source package; the journal and the year were confirmed only from the running heads (VOL. 15, NO. 19; page 444). OCR problems: red-browm (red-brown), posterior rnargin (margin), Memurements (Measurements), Bye pot (probably Eye spot) are misreadings of the scan; the measurement figures are all legible.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The species is distinguished by the soldier head capsule being densely covered with coarse long setae. Compared with M. serrula Desneux from Borneo, the soldier of this species is larger and its head capsule more densely haired (the soldier of M. serrula is small and its head capsule more sparsely haired); compared with M. annandalei Silvestri from Barkuda Island, the head capsule is also more densely haired.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule chestnut (red-brown); head length less than 2× the head width, cylindrical, the sides parallel (slightly concave at the middle); the head widest posteriorly and narrowing anteriorly, the posterior margin rounded; the epicranial suture markedly inclined forward; the head capsule densely covered with rather long setae. Fontanelle transparent, small but distinct, raised, nearly oval, situated at the origin of the epicranial suture. Eye spot distinct (the original reads "Bye pot", probably an OCR error for Eye spot), situated at the lower edge of the depression in which the antennal socket lies. Gula width at the middle slightly less than 1/2 its maximum anterior width. Labrum pale yellowish brown, wider than long, the anterior part nearly triangular, with long hairs. Mandibles dark red-brown (paler at the base), arcuate or sabre-shaped; the "bow" of the left mandible 0.6 mm deep (from the inner edge to the straight line joining the apex and the base); mandibular base broad, narrowing towards the apex, which is pointed and incurved, the inner edge of the basal 2/3 with irregular coarse teeth. Antennae yellow to pale yellowish brown, 13-segmented; the segments widening towards the apex, with long hairs; segment 3 1/2 the length of segment 2; segment 4 slightly shorter than segment 2; the terminal segment elongate, slender, nearly oval. Pronotum pale yellowish brown, saddle-shaped, the anterior and posterior margins with a shallow rounded median concavity; the sides gradually rounded and narrowed posteriorly, the margins densely covered with long hairs. Legs yellowish, slender, with long hairs. Abdomen yellowish; tergites densely covered with long hairs; cerci indistinct. Measurements: soldier total length 5.3 mm (the original notes "probably a shrunken specimen"); head length (including mandibles) 2.7 mm; head length (excluding mandibles, to the anterior margin) 1.9 mm; left mandible length 1.25 mm; pronotal length 0.3 mm; hind tibia length 0.9 mm; head width (posterior) 1.2 mm; head width (anterior) 1 mm; head height (middle) 1 mm; pronotal width 0.75 mm.
